5 I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. 6 If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned. - John 15:5-6 (KJV)

The bible uses the natural things of nature to illustrate many things, like the seeds we sow, and this illustration of us being the branches, and Jesus being the vine. We should not ever try to operate on our own, as like a branch, we need the vine (Jesus) to provide all our nourishment. If you are born again, you have Jesus living inside you (Galatians 4:6), and if you abide in Him, you will be able to produce much fruit. In our busy lives, many don’t think it is possible to always abide in Jesus, but you can by bringing every thought into obedience to Him (2 Corinthians 10:5). If we can go through the whole day worrying about a problem, then we can keep our minds upon Jesus all day. How true it is that we can do nothing without Jesus – but thank God I am never without Him (Hebrews 13:5).

The way that we abide in Jesus is to obey His commandments (Hebrews 5:9), and follow His direction given us through the Holy Spirit. Jesus has told us to love the Father and each other (Matthew 22:37-39), as well as to do the works that He did while on earth (John 14:12). If we are to work out our salvation (Philippians 2:12), then we must obey Jesus and follow the leading of the Holy Spirit in our lives, so we won’t be cast into the fire (Revelation 20:15). Even a born again Christian can be sent to hell, if they don’t follow the commands of the Holy Spirit, as that is blasphemy against the Holy Ghost (Matthew 12:31-32), and you should read the web page “New Revelations” on our web site to get an explanation of this. Praise God for giving us His Word, and all the revelations.

I get 7-12 hours depending. Without something forcing me to get up (like work), I don't get to bed till late (2-3am).

As for the bed, I need a softer bed (toss and turn on hard ones) and cold and wind (fans) help greatly. The fan also generates white noise.
"I have a nice comforter, a few cozy pillows, I usually read a chapter of a book and it's lights out by 8:30. THAT'S HOW I SLEEP AT NIGHT."

My sleep cycles are erratic, no amount of preparation or consistent attempts at a regular sleep pattern have worked. I sleep when I feel tired, I wake when I am ready. Only an event to wake up to is enough to break that.

My brain doesn't really go into REM sleep until early morning, even if I go to sleep at midnight. Found that out at a sleep clinic... so even if I go to sleep at a "normal" time and wake up at like 8AM, I'm still very tired. If I sleep from 4 to noon I am much more rested, and if I go to sleep closer to 6AM I wake up without an alarm before 8 hours have passed.

I sleep for roughly 8 hours a day. Sometimes I sleep 10 or 12 hours, sometimes 6 or so.

I make a point of getting to bed from 10PM to 2AM. Ideally I'd sleep everyday at 2AM but I'm usually tired before that. It helps a lot to have a semi-fixed schedule so your body gets used to it.

I lay belly down. Always have, always will. Always on a bed. Sleeping in a vertical position doesn't count as sleep because if you achieved full sleep/relaxation you'd wake up on the floor so it's safe to say you don't achieve deep sleep in a chair or the like.

The days when I sleep 10-12 hours are usually the days I'm tired and decide to sleep early. No people, you can't wake up 7AM everyday during the week and then go out on friday, crash at 5AM and hope to sleep for 10 hours. Only a moron will trade his health for a party - but by all means, party on if you got your sleep under control!

Another thing I do to promote my sleeping is to treat myself whenever I sleep 10 or 12 hours a day. If I sleep 10 hours I'll give myself a small treat like a chocolate bar after lunch or eating out. If I sleep 12 hours I'll make it nicer.

Sleep is very important to me - my genetics are filled with insomniacs and I've had a lot of trouble sleeping before, having to take medication and so on but by taking control over my sleep instead of giving up (oh I just can't sleep, what can I do, poor me) I figure that by now I sleep better than most people.

Also, obviously control you caffeine intake: anything more than 2 cups of coffee/1 expresso on a normal day is overdoing it for most people. If you need more advice just google "sleep hygiene".

Veronique de Rugy: The Dodd-Frank Five-Year Anniversary Is as Bad as We Thought It Would Be

The lede:

When the Dodd-Frank Act took effect on July 21, 2010, critics were fast to predict that the 2,300 page-long legislation, which passed the House without a single Republican vote and received only three GOP votes in the Senate would fail. Tomorrow will mark the five-year anniversary of Dodd-Frank and its unfortunate distorting effects. Just as when it was passed, the legislation remains unable to address the problems it was intended to.

The legislation has overwhelmed the regulatory system, stifled the financial industry, impaired economic growth, and done nothing to correct the pernicious effects of “too big to fail.” But that’s only the beginning: Many more of its regulations still need to be written, some several years down the road, all of which injects massive uncertainty into the financial industry.
